market_mood: AI/neocloud credit jitters keep tech under pressure (CoreWeave down >20% on the week) while money rotates into staples, energy and old-economy names; Middle East escalation — Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Trump floating strikes on Iran — keeps an oil and defense bid alive.
self_check: My record is best in mergers (71%) and oil/energy (66%) and weakest on high-confidence AI calls, so today I lean on a closed deal, a cash takeover spread, and refining margins rather than trying to time the AI selloff.

picks.reason: Proofpoint agreed to buy Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash in a $6.3B deal; cash deals usually keep drifting toward the offer price as the spread narrows.
KFC is switching its US restaurants from PepsiCo to Coca-Cola for the first time in decades, a visible share gain in fountain beverages that also fits the week's rotation into staples.
PepsiCo loses KFC's US beverage business to Coke, a modest but symbolic hit to its foodservice franchise after years of losing restaurant accounts.
Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Trump saying the US may need to hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain keep missile-defense and munitions demand in focus, with defense primes reporting earnings shortly.
Copart closed its acquisition of ACV Auctions, adding dealer wholesale auctions to its salvage platform; integration upside is usually underappreciated right after a close.
Exxon's preliminary numbers flagged $4.5B of extra profit from refining margins, and Middle East supply risk plus India's diesel duty cut support cracks — a direct read-through to pure-play refiners.

top_buys.pitch: Refining margins are quietly booming and Exxon just put a number on it.
top_buys.why: Exxon's preliminary third-quarter disclosure said higher refining margins added $4.5 billion to earnings, which is a direct read-through for pure-play refiners like Marathon. Oil is heading for a weekly gain on Middle East supply risk, and India cutting diesel duty supports global distillate demand. Energy was one of the strongest sectors last week, so this idea is with the tide rather than against it.
top_buys.risks: Crack spreads are volatile and can collapse quickly if crude spikes without product prices following, and a Middle East de-escalation would take risk premium out of the whole complex.
top_buys.watch: Marathon's own Q3 earnings and weekly US refining margin and inventory data.

top_buys.pitch: A $49.75 all-cash takeover gives a floor and a predictable drift toward the deal price.
top_buys.why: Proofpoint agreed to buy Varonis in a $6.3 billion all-cash deal, which removes most fundamental risk from the stock. Shares typically trade a few percent below the offer until closing, and that gap narrows over time. My merger-arb style calls have been my best-performing category.
top_buys.risks: Antitrust or financing delays can widen the spread, and a deal break would send the stock sharply lower toward its pre-announcement price.
top_buys.watch: Regulatory filings and any second-request news on the Proofpoint deal.

top_buys.pitch: Winning KFC's US fountain business from Pepsi is a durable, visible share gain in a sector money is rotating into.
top_buys.why: KFC is moving its US restaurants to Coca-Cola for the first time in decades, adding thousands of outlets to Coke's foodservice network and reinforcing its dominance in restaurant pours. Consumer Staples was the best sector last week (+4.8%) as investors fled tech, so the flow backdrop helps. The financial impact is modest but the narrative momentum tends to persist for weeks.
top_buys.risks: The revenue impact is small relative to Coke's size, and a sharp tech rebound could reverse the defensive rotation that is supporting staples.
top_buys.watch: Coca-Cola's upcoming quarterly results and commentary on North America foodservice volumes.

top_buys.pitch: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and US strike talk on Iran keep the air-defense order book filling.
top_buys.why: Trump said the US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, and the Houthis are hitting Saudi Arabia and Yemen's presidential palace effectively, which drives demand for interceptors and missile defense that RTX supplies. Norway's $2 trillion wealth fund may also lift its ban on defense names, a potential new source of buying. Defense primes report earnings in the coming days, giving a near-term catalyst.
top_buys.risks: Defense momentum has been weak lately and a ceasefire or earnings disappointment on program margins could stall the stock.
top_buys.watch: RTX's Q3 earnings and any actual US military action against Iran.

top_buys.pitch: Copart just closed the ACV Auctions deal, expanding from salvage into dealer wholesale auctions.
top_buys.why: The acquisition completed today gives Copart a digital dealer-to-dealer marketplace that complements its salvage auction dominance, and integration synergies tend to be recognized slowly rather than on day one. Copart is an old-economy, cash-generative name of the type benefiting from the rotation out of tech. The deal closing removes uncertainty that had hung over the stock.
top_buys.risks: Integration costs could weigh on margins near term, and Copart's valuation leaves little room for execution slips.
top_buys.watch: Management commentary on ACV integration and synergies at the next quarterly report.
